checks.note: The program didn't save a picture with --screenshot. The operation was cancelled. Give the program a `--screenshot <file.png>` option: start normally, draw about 120 frames, save the window's picture as a PNG to that file and exit. With the option, open the window without taking focus, so a check never gets in the way of what the person is doing, and on Windows also behind other windows (a covered window still draws there; on macOS and Linux it may stop drawing, so don't lower it there). Keep it drawing while it isn't focused, or the picture never comes. In egui: `ViewportBuilder::with_active(false)`, on Windows `with_window_level(WindowLevel::AlwaysOnBottom)`, and on macOS `with_activate_ignoring_other_apps(false)` through `NativeOptions::event_loop_builder`; in Unity, `Application.runInBackground = true`; other stacks, their own way. Started without the option, the program opens as usual. Craft Anything runs it that way after each build to check the result, and a build without the option, or with a blank picture, doesn't pass. Try it yourself: run it with a file inside app/ (for example app/shots/now.png) and check that it saves the picture.
